The check starts when Next.js calls `register()` in [src/instrumentation.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/5e918d94-d789-4e98-90b2-9d9977690b57/src/instrumentation.ts). In the Node runtime, it registers event handlers and starts the in-process scheduler. `startScheduler()` in [src/server/jobs/scheduler.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/5e918d94-d789-4e98-90b2-9d9977690b57/src/server/jobs/scheduler.ts) calls `tick()` every minute; the overdue job has a 60-minute cadence and is due on the first tick. `tick()` enqueues it, and `drain()` and `runHandler()` in [src/server/jobs/queue.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/5e918d94-d789-4e98-90b2-9d9977690b57/src/server/jobs/queue.ts) dispatch it to `runOverdueIssueJob()`. A secret-checked `POST` to [src/app/api/cron/overdue/route.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/5e918d94-d789-4e98-90b2-9d9977690b57/src/app/api/cron/overdue/route.ts) can also invoke the job directly.

`runOverdueIssueJob(now)` in [src/server/jobs/overdue-issue-job.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/5e918d94-d789-4e98-90b2-9d9977690b57/src/server/jobs/overdue-issue-job.ts) first checks that archived issues should be filtered. It asks `listOrgIdsForRollup()` in [src/server/repositories/usage-repository.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/5e918d94-d789-4e98-90b2-9d9977690b57/src/server/repositories/usage-repository.ts) for up to 50 organization IDs from usage records, ordered by measurement time. For each, `listOverdueIssues()` in [src/server/repositories/issue-repository.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/5e918d94-d789-4e98-90b2-9d9977690b57/src/server/repositories/issue-repository.ts) selects that organization’s unarchived issues with a non-null `dueAt` strictly earlier than `now`, and status `backlog`, `todo`, `in_progress`, or `in_review`.

For each selected issue, the job emits `issue.overdue` with the organization, issue, project, due date and assignee IDs, a null actor, and the check time. It owns the scan and announcement, not recipient selection or notification delivery. Its module-level `reported` set suppresses another announcement for the same issue ID after `emit()` returns; failures caught by the job increment its failure count without adding the ID. This is **process-lifetime deduplication**, not a durable exactly-once guarantee: a restart clears the set, and concurrent scans can race. Also, `emit()` in [src/lib/event-bus.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/5e918d94-d789-4e98-90b2-9d9977690b57/src/lib/event-bus.ts) isolates subscriber failures and does not rethrow them, so an issue can be marked reported even if notification handling failed.

At startup, [src/server/services/event-registry.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/5e918d94-d789-4e98-90b2-9d9977690b57/src/server/services/event-registry.ts) imports [notification-service.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/5e918d94-d789-4e98-90b2-9d9977690b57/src/server/services/notification-service.ts), whose `registerFanOut()` subscribes to the event. Its handler skips an unassigned issue; otherwise it calls `notify()` for the single assignee, with an overdue title, due-date body, and issue link. `notify()` looks up that person’s preference for `issue_overdue` in the organization through `getPreference()` in [notification-preference-repository.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/5e918d94-d789-4e98-90b2-9d9977690b57/src/server/repositories/notification-preference-repository.ts). `resolveChannels()` defaults to `in_app` and `email` when there is no preference; for a stored preference it includes in-app when enabled, and email when enabled and either `digestOnly` is false or the `digest_email` flag is enabled. If no channels remain, no row is created. Otherwise `insertNotifications()` in [notification-repository.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/5e918d94-d789-4e98-90b2-9d9977690b57/src/server/repositories/notification-repository.ts) persists an unread row for that recipient with the selected channels.

The implemented delivery has limits. The fan-out records the email channel but does not itself send an immediate overdue email. For digest subscribers, `runDigestEmailJob()` in [digest-email-job.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/5e918d94-d789-4e98-90b2-9d9977690b57/src/server/jobs/digest-email-job.ts) runs during the organization’s configured UTC hour when the plan flag permits it. `buildDigest()` in [digest-service.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/5e918d94-d789-4e98-90b2-9d9977690b57/src/server/services/digest-service.ts) collects the recipient’s unread rows in the window, and the job looks up their email address, renders the digest, calls `sendEmail()`, and marks included rows read. That digest query does not filter entries by their recorded channels. Finally, `sendEmail()` in [email-service.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/5e918d94-d789-4e98-90b2-9d9977690b57/src/server/services/email-service.ts) logs the draft’s metadata; the application has no outbound mail transport.
